newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine vice PM sees no Tbill limit for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine vice PM sees no Tbill limit for foreigners.

text.p: Viktor Pynzenyk, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of reforms, said on Saturday that Ukraine would not impose limits on foreigners participating in its lucrative Treasury-bill market.
"Limitations do not work. Western investors have different ways of working and if there are any bans they will get round them," Pynzenyk told reporters in his office.

He said Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko had ordered him to find a way of ensuring even issues of the high-yield paper, which have proved so popular that the flood of foreign investors helped push the hryvnia currency to near-record highs last week.
"That is investors will be offered a set volume, which has been clearly specified beforehand," he said.

Issues have fluctuated wildly in volume from as low as 20 million hryvnias to 200 million hryvnias in the last few months, when non-residents have become particularly active, drawn by yields which varied from 30 to 40 percent last week.

Pynzenyk said the government could advertise its auctions in advance and keep the volume of paper offered stable to avoid big fluctuations in the hryvnia, which started the week at 1.85 per dollar and finished it at 1.765.
The finance ministry tells the central bank when it wants to issue paper, which then informs banks by electronic mail the evening before the twice-weekly auctions.
Pynzenyk, running reforms in a country even he conceded needed to eradicate corruption, made clear Ukraine wanted to attract funds from all kinds of foreign investor.
He said a new reform package making its way through parliament included big improvements for foreign investors.
For example, a rule forcing Ukrainian enterprises to obtain a licence before receiving foreign investment would be scrapped if the law was passed, he said.
"I see no reason to license the receipt of such credits. Except one. Corruption."
